title: Gate: --fail-on-severity, --fail-on-count and [gate] in Scan.toml
description: Each sub folder is its own package with 1 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM and 3 LOW issues. A tripped gate exits 1 after the reports are written; it never removes issues from the output or the reports. Not available before 0.13.0. Each gate option on the command line replaces only its own field of [gate] in Scan.toml, and warns only when Scan.toml writes that field with a different value.

steps.name: No gate
steps.note: Findings alone never fail the scan.

steps.name: --fail-on-severity=HIGH
steps.note: Fails: 1 issue at or above HIGH.

steps.name: --fail-on-severity=medium --fail-on-count=3
steps.note: Fails: HIGH 1 + MEDIUM 2 reaches 3. The severity is case-insensitive.

steps.name: --exclude-rules + gate
steps.note: Passes: the gate counts only the issues left after rule selection.

steps.name: --fail-on-severity=NONE overrides Scan.toml
steps.note: Passes, with a warning: --fail-on-severity=NONE overrides [gate] failOnSeverity = "HIGH" in Scan.toml.

steps.name: --fail-on-count=2 replaces only failOnCount
steps.note: The severity HIGH is kept from Scan.toml: 1 HIGH issue, below the count of 2, passes. No warning, since Scan.toml does not write failOnCount.

steps.name: --fail-on-severity=LOW --fail-on-count=2
steps.note: One warning for failOnSeverity only; 6 issues at or above LOW, fails.

steps.name: Invalid [gate] values and keys
steps.note: Scan.toml has 3 errors, each with its line and column; nothing is scanned.
